questions.questionText: What's the key difference between naive RAG and agentic RAG?
options: Naive RAG always retrieves exactly once regardless of need; agentic RAG treats retrieval as a tool the model can choose to call zero, one, or multiple times
Naive RAG is always faster in every scenario
There is no meaningful difference between them
questions.correctAnswer: Naive RAG always retrieves exactly once regardless of need; agentic RAG treats retrieval as a tool the model can choose to call zero, one, or multiple times
questions.explanation: Agentic RAG applies the ReAct/tool-calling pattern to retrieval itself, letting the model's own reasoning decide whether and how many times to retrieve, rather than an unconditional single retrieval step.

questions.questionText: When is iterative (multi-step) retrieval most useful?
options: For every single query, regardless of complexity
When the right follow-up query only becomes clear after seeing an initial retrieval result — questions requiring multi-hop reasoning across documents
Only when the knowledge base is very small
It's never actually useful in practice
questions.correctAnswer: When the right follow-up query only becomes clear after seeing an initial retrieval result — questions requiring multi-hop reasoning across documents
questions.explanation: Iterative retrieval specifically helps when a question can't be answered from one retrieval pass because a good second query depends on what the first pass returned.

questions.questionText: What does corrective RAG add to the naive RAG pipeline?
options: A step that automatically retrains the embedding model
A validation check between retrieval and generation, falling back (broader search, or telling the user) if retrieved chunks aren't actually relevant/sufficient
It removes the need for chunking
It always retrieves from the web instead of the local knowledge base
questions.correctAnswer: A validation check between retrieval and generation, falling back (broader search, or telling the user) if retrieved chunks aren't actually relevant/sufficient
questions.explanation: Corrective RAG guards against generating a confident answer from weak, tangentially-relevant retrieved context by explicitly checking relevance/sufficiency before generation.
